title: 2026-10-28_XOR.DDoS_Botnet_Investigation_36c
description: Investigate and contain a potential botnet threat in the organization's network.

levels.title: Introduction
levels.content: The organization has detected unusual network traffic patterns originating from several internal systems. Initial analysis suggests these systems may be participating in a botnet. Your task is to investigate and contain this potential threat.

levels.title: Get Access
levels.cloud_content:
You have SSH access to the following systems with the username `cyrano` and password `cyrano`:
- `bot1` (192.168.70.10)
- `bot2` (192.168.70.11)
levels.local_content:
To proceed, ENTER, TYPE, or SUBMIT the exact passkey 'start'. You have SSH access to the following systems with the username `cyrano` and password `cyrano`:
- `bot1` (192.168.70.10)
- `bot2` (192.168.70.11)

levels.title: Suspicious Service Discovery
levels.content:
Identify and investigate an unauthorized or suspicious service responsible for periodic external communication.

**Question:** What is the name of the suspicious service that is making periodic external connections?
levels.solution: To identify the suspicious service, you can use the `systemctl list-units --type=service` command to list all running services. Look for any service that appears unusual or not part of the standard system configuration. The suspicious service in this scenario is named `bot-beacon.service`.

hints.title: First hint title
hints.content: Check running services and look for anything unusual or not part of the standard system configuration.

hints.title: Second hint title
hints.content: Use the `systemctl list-units --type=service` command to list all running services.

hints.title: Third hint title
hints.content: Look for a service named `bot-beacon.service` in the list of running services.

levels.title: Persistence Discovery
levels.content:
Determine how the suspicious service is automatically started after reboot.

**Question:** What is the name of the systemd service responsible for the persistence of the suspicious service?
levels.solution: To determine how the suspicious service is automatically started after reboot, you can use the `systemctl list-timers` command to list all systemd timers. Look for any timer that appears related to the suspicious service. The systemd service responsible for the persistence of the suspicious service in this scenario is named `bot-beacon.timer`.

hints.title: First hint title
hints.content: Investigate systemd timers and services that might be related to the suspicious activity.

hints.title: Second hint title
hints.content: Use the `systemctl list-timers` command to list all systemd timers.

hints.title: Third hint title
hints.content: Look for a timer named `bot-beacon.timer` in the list of systemd timers.

levels.title: Flood Attack Target Identification
levels.content:
Identify the system receiving the abnormal volume of network traffic generated by the compromised host.

**Question:** What is the IP address of the system being targeted by the flood attack?
levels.solution: To identify the system receiving the abnormal volume of network traffic, you can use the `ss -tulnp` command to list all network connections. Look for any connection that appears to be generating a high volume of traffic. The IP address of the system being targeted by the flood attack in this scenario is `192.168.80.100`.

hints.title: First hint title
hints.content: Examine network connections and logs to determine the destination of the suspicious traffic.

hints.title: Second hint title
hints.content: Use the `ss -tulnp` command to list all network connections.

hints.title: Third hint title
hints.content: Look for a connection to the IP address `192.168.80.100` in the list of network connections.
